title: Onboarding and Rollout Playbook
summary: Operational rollout guide for launching RAPTOR to new teams and scaling usage safely.

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Successful rollout depends on data quality and access governance before broad onboarding. Do not start with open-ended user provisioning.

sections.title: Rollout objective
paragraphs: The rollout objective is to make RAPTOR operationally trustworthy from day one for inventory, pentest execution, and reporting. This requires a phased rollout that validates users, taxonomy, and workflow quality before scale-up.
Treat rollout as an operations program, not a UI onboarding event. The target outcome is stable weekly use with predictable ownership, assignment, and reporting behavior.

rows: Authentication connectivity
Users cannot onboard without working local or LDAP auth path.
Admin and at least one non-admin user can login successfully.
Permission baseline
Wrong role defaults block critical workflows.
Each target role can access expected modules and no more.
Source and taxonomy setup
Dashboards and findings become noisy without stable taxonomy.
IP sources and vulnerability categories are configured and reviewed.
Template baseline
Report and checklist output quality depends on templates.
Default templates load, customizations validated on sample records.
Data ingestion health
Users lose trust if inventory is stale or inconsistent.
Manual update succeeds and records appear current.

sections.title: Pilot rollout sequence
paragraphs: Start with a small controlled cohort, then expand by role and application domain after measurable stability.
orderedList: Select pilot scope with one admin, one manager, one pentester, and one inventory user.
Assign pilot applications and records with clear owner and maintainer metadata.
Execute one full pentest lifecycle from `Not Started` to report generation.
Run weekly review using dashboard signals and fix observed workflow friction.
Document issues and update taxonomy, templates, or permissions before expansion.
Expand cohort in batches, repeating the same lifecycle validation gates.

rows: Admin
`Settings`, `Dashboard`
User lifecycle, taxonomy governance, maintenance controls, and recovery procedures.
Manager
`Dashboard`, `Records`, `Security`
Prioritization, assignment governance, KPI interpretation, and escalation decisions.
Pentester
`Security`, `Pentest Record`, `Reporting`
Lifecycle updates, findings quality, checklist completion, and report generation.
User
`Records`
Metadata quality, ownership fields, filtering, and export for operational handoff.

sections.title: Baseline configuration checklist
orderedList: Create user accounts with minimal required roles and optional permissions.
Validate `Settings` section visibility matches policy per role.
Configure IP source mappings for known ingestion origins.
Review vulnerability category list and remove ambiguous duplicates.
Validate checklist and report templates with a test record.
Verify session timeout, extension, and lockout behavior in a controlled test.
Record baseline configuration snapshot for audit and rollback reference.

rows: Access gate
Each role can complete its core workflow without unauthorized errors.
Data gate
Pilot records have complete owner, maintainer, application, and source metadata.
Security gate
At least one complete pentest lifecycle has been executed and validated.
Reporting gate
Generated report output is accurate and accepted by stakeholders.
Operational gate
Known issues are documented with owner and target resolution date.

sections.title: Steady-state improvement loop
paragraphs: After go-live, move to a recurring operations loop focused on quality drift detection and process improvement. Keep scope changes incremental and measurable.
Use dashboard and activity signals to detect backlog risk, ownership gaps, and slow remediation. Feed results back into role training and configuration governance.
orderedList: Run weekly manager review of coverage, open risk, and assignment balance.
Run monthly admin review of permissions, taxonomy, and template drift.
Run quarterly restore and recovery validation for continuity readiness.
Track action items and completion in an operational governance register.
